title: Synchronization points: growth, asymptotics, congruences, and the synchronization zeta function: the form of the synchronization zeta function for two permutations of a finite set (printed as Theorem 30)
author: Alexander Fel'shtyn, Mateusz Slomiany
work: Synchronization points: growth, asymptotics, congruences, and the synchronization zeta function
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 3.1 (source0.tex lines 1361--1375, source label thm:synchronization-zeta-form-bijections-finite), the explicit factorisation of the synchronization zeta function of two permutations of a finite set into the linear factors (1-z) and (1+z) and the quadratic factors built from the real parts of the L-th roots of unity, with real exponents. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1376--1466 (91 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the two results the proof invokes. The proof is a genuine structural argument rather than a computation: it exploits the periodicity of the sequence of synchronization numbers established earlier in the article, decomposes the zeta function according to the orbit structure forced by the finite orders of the two permutations, groups the orbits by the roots of unity that govern their growth, and identifies the exponents of the linear and quadratic factors, treating the case of an even common period separately because it produces the additional linear factor (1+z). The substantive steps are the grouping of the periodic data by roots of unity and the extraction of the exponents in both parity cases. H3: a complete original research-paper proof of a main structural theorem of the paper, with every invoked result delivered.
